proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnification section at all, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 20.5). We have inserted a new Section 20 giving us a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of law, Vendor-caused data breaches and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard procedure, customary IP exclusions and infringement remedies, and a narrow reciprocal indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

ops.text: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

20.2 Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that content or materials provided by Customer to Vendor for use in the Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, provided that delayed notice reduces the indemnifying Party's obligations only to the extent it is prejudiced. The indemnifying Party controls the defence and settlement with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. No settlement that admits liability or imposes any obligation on the indemnified Party is effective without its prior written consent.

20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables without Vendor's authorization, combination of the Services or Deliverables with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent that combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

20.5 If an infringement claim is made or reasonably anticipated, Vendor shall, at its expense and at Customer's election where practicable, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected Services or Deliverables, or modify or replace them with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing alternative. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion and Fees paid for Deliverables Customer can no longer use. These remedies are in addition to Vendor's obligations under Section 20.1.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 20 (Indemnification) with a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, a narrow Customer indemnity, standard procedure, IP exclusions, and infringement remedies (resolving the dangling cross-reference in Section 9.3 to Section 20.5).

We inserted a new Section 20 with the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions, and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at 20.5 (which also repairs the broken cross-reference), plus a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

No competing or one-sided liability limit appears in the warranty, indemnity or insurance provisions (18.2 expressly states insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). No redline needed.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A successor (notice only). 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without our consent (reasonableness standard) and never to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1 because it is expressly limited to "other assignments" (i.e., those outside the 24.1 carve-out) and applies mutually with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard. Section 13.3 tracks Section 24 by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a permitted assignment. A document-wide search for "change of control" and "assign" surfaced no deemed-assignment trigger or Vendor exit/re-pricing right; 9.2's insolvency clause is mutual and expressly excludes lawful reorganizations that do not impair performance. No redline needed.

quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Compliant; the failed period check is a phrasing false negative. The Deliverable conformity period in 19.2 is written out as "ninety days" rather than "90 days", but it is exactly the 90-day floor in our preferred position and it runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, so it is measured more favourably to us than a pure delivery-date trigger. The software-side warranty is longer still: hosted Services must conform "throughout the subscription term", and under § 8.1 the Agreement runs for three years, so the hosted conformity commitment is expressed in years and exceeds the 12-month software benchmark. Section 19.1 adds an untimed professional and workmanlike services warranty against industry standards, this Agreement and each Order Form, and 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty (the "intentionally introduced by Vendor" qualifier is a standard market limitation and does not undercut the position). Section 19.4 gives the required remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid, and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Section 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and confirms that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties. No redline is warranted; if the numeral form matters for internal consistency, the period could be conformed at signature to "ninety (90) days" as a purely clerical change.
